name: Wedgwood Blue
lede: Wedgwood blue is a very pale, slightly violet blue whose name comes from ceramics; in our data it is a Ridgway 1912 name.

sections.title: A potter's blue
sections.body:
The name points to ceramics. In Garfield's account of a Bureau of Standards count of 7,500 color names, "Wedgwood blue" is the example given for the ceramic category, which held 36 names [1]. That is the only mention of the name in the color books we searched, so what follows rests mostly on our own records.

The swatch is a very light purplish blue, ISCC-NBS block 185, about 2.8 units from its nearest standard name [2]. It sits close to [[powder-blue]] and [[sky-blue]] in lightness, with a slight lean toward violet [2].

sections.title: First on paper in 1912
sections.body:
Our earliest written record of the name is Ridgway's 1912 color nomenclature, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system lists it again [2]. That is a record date for the name in our sources, not proof of when potters first used the blue [2].

In the archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color this pale appears in 25 paintings, most often as a hidden color rather than a main one [3]. The earliest match is a 1474 Piero della Francesca panel, a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not a Wedgwood connection [3].

origin.named_after: English Wedgwood pottery (Garfield files the name under ceramics)

questions.q: In Garfield's count of color names, which category holds Wedgwood blue?
True or false: the 1474 painting match proves Wedgwood-style blue existed then.

openers: Garfield gives Wedgwood blue as the example of a ceramic color name.
